basics.name: Leilany Torres Diaz
basics.label: Research Associate & Data Analyst
basics.summary: Research assistant and data analyst with experience in neuroimaging pipelines, machine-learning-based neural decoding, and computational psychiatry methods. Experienced in reproducible analysis code, complex fMRI and behavioral datasets, and research support from data collection through presentation.

work.name: Kempner Institute, Harvard University
highlights: Built and maintained Python pipelines to preprocess, parcellate, and analyze fMRI datasets.
Benchmarked deep vision models against neural responses across visual-cortex regions.
Used representational similarity analysis, cross-validated model selection, and bootstrapped confidence intervals in reproducible Jupyter workflows.
Managed analysis code with GitHub and documented pipelines for collaborators.
Designed behavioral experiments on visual memorability and object recognition, including power analyses and study-design refinement.

work.name: Phelps Memory Lab, Harvard University and Kredlow Lab, Tufts University
highlights: Support research activities across the Phelps and Kredlow labs.
Complete training in fMRI acquisition and fMRI preprocessing.

work.name: Norcal Brain Center
highlights: Collected, organized, and maintained clinical data for more than 20 patients per day across traumatic brain injury, autism, anxiety, and depression presentations.
Communicated neurophysiology and neurofeedback concepts to patients and families while supporting protocol adherence and engagement.

work.name: Independent Tutoring
highlights: Tutored students in chemistry, calculus, STEM subjects, and Spanish using individualized study plans.

projects.name: rsFC Predictive Modeling Pipeline
projects.description: Resting-state functional-connectivity classification pipeline using fMRI data.
highlights: Built a Python pipeline to classify healthy controls and bipolar-disorder participants using resting-state fMRI connectivity from the UCLA CNP dataset.
Used Yeo-Schaefer parcellations, linear SVM classification, and five-fold cross-validation.
Achieved 73 percent accuracy with a permutation-test result of p = 0.021 and visualized 77 network-level feature weights.

projects.name: DNN-Brain Alignment Benchmark
projects.description: Benchmark of deep neural networks against fMRI responses across ventral-stream regions.
highlights: Evaluated 30 models on fMRI data from 10 participants and 72 stimuli using representational similarity analysis.
Used split-half cross-validation for layer selection and bootstrapped confidence intervals.
Found AlexNet matched or outperformed modern architectures across ventral-stream regions.

projects.name: Aversive Learning Extension
projects.description: Computational psychiatry project examining anxiety and avoidance mechanisms.
highlights: Extended a behavioral paradigm with reinforcement-learning models, Bayesian parameter recovery, hierarchical model fitting, and posterior predictive checks.
Introduced and evaluated a hesitation parameter to represent decision uncertainty in aversive learning.

publications.name: Ventral Stream Responses to Inanimate Objects Are Equally Aligned with AlexNet 2012 and Modern Deep Neural Networks
publications.summary: Torres Diaz, L., and Alvarez, G. A. Poster presented at CCN, Amsterdam, 2025.

highlights: Recruited speakers, authored technical newsletters, and coordinated a weekly seminar series for 10 months.
